title: Veterinary and Pet Care Business
desc: Start and run a small pet care business, from grooming, boarding and walking to records, hygiene and when to refer to a vet.
outcomes: Explain animal welfare needs and the limits of a non-vet service.
Run safe handling, hygiene and booking steps.
Judge risks, bites, disease and legal duties.
task: Plan and pilot a small pet care service with welfare rules, hygiene plan, booking and price sheet, owner forms and emergency steps.
condition: Practice animals from willing owners or a shelter partner, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor veterinarian. Medical treatments are for qualified vets only.
standard: Every pet has an owner form and vaccine record; welfare needs are met; injuries and bites have a response plan; costs and price are shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Pet lovers, vet clinic assistants, groomers, walkers and boarders.
evidence: service menu, owner form, hygiene plan, price sheet, pilot log
modules: Welfare basics
Understand
Every animal needs the same five things, no matter the species.
A suitable environment, a suitable diet, the ability to behave normally, appropriate company or separation, and protection from pain, suffering and disease.
Signs of stress: panting, hiding, shaking, aggression, changes in appetite.
Never leave animals in hot vehicles or without water.
Know the needs of each species you handle.
A dog left in shade with fresh water stays calm. One left in a parked car on a warm day can suffer heatstroke within minutes.
Write a welfare card for two species covering the five needs.
Each need is covered and accurate.
Owner forms and records
Apply
You must know the pet and the owner before you take responsibility.
Collect pet name, age, vaccines, medicines, allergies, behaviour notes, vet contact and emergency contact.
Written consent for care and for emergency treatment with a spending limit.
Keep records secure and up to date.
Decline animals when records or vaccines are missing.
A boarding form shows an unvaccinated puppy. The business declines the booking and advises the owner to vaccinate.
Design an owner form and fill it for a practice pet.
Includes vaccine, vet, emergency and consent fields.
Safe handling
Apply
Protect animals and people.
Approach calmly; read body language; do not corner an animal.
Use correct leads, harnesses and carriers and keep species apart.
Know basic first aid for bites and scratches and report them.
Train in handling under a mentor.
A walker uses a double lead and keeps a distance from a nervous dog near traffic, preventing a bolt.
Practise handling steps under a mentor and complete an observation sheet.
Mentor sees safe handling with no incidents.
Hygiene and disease control
Apply
Clean spaces prevent disease.
Clean and disinfect kennels, bowls and tools between animals.
Isolate any animal that coughs, vomits or has diarrhoea and call the vet.
Wash hands, handle waste safely and control pests.
Keep a cleaning log.
A cough in one dog leads to isolation, a vet call and disinfecting shared areas, preventing an outbreak.
Create a daily hygiene plan and log.
Plan lists frequency, method and responsible person.
When to refer to a vet
Evaluate
A pet business is not a veterinary clinic.
Poisoning, injury, breathing trouble, long vomiting, seizures and collapse need a vet at once.
Do not give medicines unless the owner or vet instructs in writing.
Keep the clinic number and an emergency clinic number visible.
Record time and symptoms.
A boarder calls the vet within 10 minutes after a dog eats chocolate, following a pre-agreed plan.
Write an emergency card with numbers, steps and owner contacts.
Card is tested in a mock call.
Services, scheduling and pricing
Analyse
Match services to capacity and cost.
Services: grooming, walking, day care, boarding.
Time per pet plus cleaning plus travel.
Costs: staff, supplies, transport, insurance, space.
Price to cover costs and margin.
A 60-minute groom takes 90 minutes of table time. At 400 INR per hour of staff plus 120 INR of supplies, the price is set at 1,100 INR.
Cost three services and set prices.
Totals correct and currency shown.
Law, insurance and ethics
Evaluate
Know the rules before you start.
Business licence, animal-welfare law and insurance.
No cruelty or neglect; report abuse.
Honest advertising and clear terms.
Respect owners' privacy.
A provider takes public-liability insurance before accepting clients and keeps the policy on file.
List the rules for your place with sources.
Each rule has a source and date.
Pilot and improve
Create
Run 30 days with a small number of clients.
Track bookings, complaints, injuries and rebookings.
Fix the top three issues.
Plan owner education and community links.
Review weekly.
Rebookings reach 55% after owners receive a report card with a photo after each visit.
Present your pilot review.
Numbers are real and fixes dated.
quiz: Name the five welfare needs.
Food and water, shelter, health, behaviour, company. (Covered in module 1: Welfare basics. To pass that module: Each need is covered.)
Why vaccine records?
To protect other animals. (Covered in module 2: Owner forms and records. To pass that module: Includes vaccine and vet details.)
Name a stress sign.
Panting, hiding or aggression. (Covered in module 3: Safe handling. To pass that module: Mentor observes without safety issues.)
When call a vet?
Poisoning, injury, breathing trouble, seizures, long vomiting. (Covered in module 4: Hygiene and disease control. To pass that module: Plan lists frequency and method.)
Can you give medicine freely?
No, only as the owner or vet instructs in writing. (Covered in module 5: When to refer to a vet. To pass that module: Includes numbers, steps and owner contacts.)
What goes on an owner form?
Details, vaccines, medicines, allergies, contacts, consent. (Covered in module 6: Services, scheduling and pricing. To pass that module: Totals correct; currency shown.)
Why separate sick animals?
To stop spread. (Covered in module 7: Law, insurance and ethics. To pass that module: Sources listed.)
Why insurance?
To cover injuries or damage. (Covered in module 8: Pilot and improve. To pass that module: Numbers real; fixes dated.)
What is table time?
Time in the room including cleaning. (Covered in module 8: Pilot and improve. To pass that module: Numbers real; fixes dated.)
What do you track in a pilot?
Bookings, complaints, injuries, rebookings. (Covered in module 8: Pilot and improve. To pass that module: Numbers real; fixes dated.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others

ladder: Welfare basics

L1: learner can name pet needs. Focus module: Welfare basics (Understand, 4 h). Five needs: food and water, shelter, health, behaviour and company. Key points: Know species needs and daily routines. Signs of stress: panting, hiding, aggression. Never leave animals in hot vehicles.

Teach: open with the worked example. A dog left in shade with fresh water stays calm; one in a parked car does not. Then set the activity: Write a welfare card for two species. Mark against the standard: Each need is covered. Check at this level: Name the five welfare needs. Model answer: Food and water, shelter, health, behaviour, company. Show care card.
Owner forms and records

L2: learner knows hygiene and referral limits. Focus module: Owner forms and records (Apply, 4 h). Know the pet before you take it. Key points: Name, age, vaccines, medicines, allergies, vet contact, emergency contact. Written consent for care and emergency treatment. Keep records securely.

Teach: open with the worked example. A boarding form shows an unvaccinated pup, so it is declined. Then set the activity: Design an owner form. Mark against the standard: Includes vaccine and vet details. Check at this level: Why vaccine records? Model answer: To protect other animals. Explain limits.
Safe handling

L3: learner can handle one pet safely. Focus module: Safe handling (Apply, 5 h). Protect animals and people. Key points: Approach calmly; read body language. Use correct leads and carriers; keep species apart. First-aid for bites and scratches; report them.

Teach: open with the worked example. A walker uses a double lead near traffic. Then set the activity: Practise handling steps. Mark against the standard: Mentor observes without safety issues. Check at this level: Name a stress sign. Model answer: Panting, hiding or aggression. Practise handling.
Hygiene and disease control

L4: learner can run a pet service day. Focus module: Hygiene and disease control (Apply, 4 h). Clean spaces prevent disease. Key points: Clean and disinfect kennels, tools and bowls between animals. Separate sick animals. Safe waste and hand washing.

Teach: open with the worked example. A cough in one dog leads to isolation and a vet call. Then set the activity: Create a daily hygiene plan. Mark against the standard: Plan lists frequency and method. Check at this level: When call a vet? Model answer: Poisoning, injury, breathing trouble, seizures, long vomiting. Role-play.
When to refer to a vet

L5: learner can cost and price. Focus module: When to refer to a vet (Evaluate, 4 h). Know your limits. Key points: Poisoning, injury, breathing trouble, long vomiting, seizures need a vet at once. Do not give medicines unless a vet or owner instructs in writing. Keep the clinic number visible.

Teach: open with the worked example. A boarder calls the vet within 10 minutes for a dog that ate chocolate. Then set the activity: Write an emergency card. Mark against the standard: Includes numbers, steps and owner contacts. Check at this level: Can you give medicine freely? Model answer: No, only as the owner or vet instructs in writing. Cost sheet.
Law, insurance and ethics

L6: learner can lead a small team. Focus module: Law, insurance and ethics (Evaluate, 4 h). Check licences and duties. Key points: Business licence, animal-welfare rules and insurance. No cruelty or neglect; report abuse. Honest advertising.

Teach: open with the worked example. A provider obtains public-liability insurance before taking clients. Then set the activity: List rules for your place. Mark against the standard: Sources listed. Check at this level: What goes on an owner form? Model answer: Details, vaccines, medicines, allergies, contacts, consent. Cover rota.
Pilot and improve

L7: learner can audit a service. Focus module: Pilot and improve (Create, 5 h). Run 30 days with a few clients. Key points: Track bookings, complaints, injuries, rebookings. Fix top 3 issues. Plan owner education and community tie-ups.

Teach: open with the worked example. Rebookings reach 55% after report cards with photos. Then set the activity: Present your review. Mark against the standard: Numbers real; fixes dated. Check at this level: Why separate sick animals? Model answer: To stop spread. Peer audit.
